events.title: First commercial C++ compiler
events.summary: Bjarne Stroustrup shipped Cfront 1.0 in October 1985 — the first commercial C++ compiler translating C++ to C, complementing the language's earlier public definition.
events.about: C++ adds classes and abstraction on top of C while keeping performance. Used for browsers (Chrome), game engines (Unreal), databases, trading systems, and large desktop apps. If you need C speed with OOP, teams still reach for C++.

narrative.whyChosen: C++ brought object-oriented and systems abstractions to the C ecosystem without breaking its performance model.
narrative.whyImportant: Commercial availability turned 'C with Classes' into a language teams could adopt on real projects.
narrative.problemSolved: Simula-style OOP existed, but systems programmers needed OOP that compiled down to efficient C.

events.title: FTP standardized
events.summary: RFC 959 defined the File Transfer Protocol in October 1985 — the standard for uploading and downloading files over TCP.
events.about: FTP uses separate control and data connections — clients log in, navigate directories with `CWD` and `LIST`, and transfer files with `RETR`/`STOR`. Though largely replaced by HTTPS and SFTP for security, FTP powered early web hosting, software mirrors, and embedded device updates for decades.

narrative.whyChosen: RFC 959 unified decades of ad-hoc file transfer into one interoperable internet protocol.
narrative.whyImportant: FTP was how software, patches, and media moved across the early internet before the web dominated.
narrative.problemSolved: Every host had incompatible file transfer commands; the internet needed a common client-server file protocol.

events.title: Bjarne Stroustrup releases C++
events.summary: Bjarne Stroustrup released C++ 1.0 in October 1985 — adding object-oriented features to C for systems programming.
events.about: C++ powers game engines, browsers, databases, and embedded systems — the default when C needs abstraction without garbage collection. Stroustrup's 'C with classes' became one of the most influential language designs ever.

narrative.whyChosen: C++ defined systems programming with OOP for decades before Rust's rise.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed zero-cost abstractions could compile to efficient machine code.
narrative.problemSolved: C lacked abstraction mechanisms for large simulation and systems codebases at Bell Labs.

sources.title: Stroustrup — A History of C++ (first commercial release 1985)

events.title: Richard Stallman founds FSF
events.summary: Richard Stallman founded the Free Software Foundation on October 4, 1985 — the nonprofit behind GNU and the GPL.
events.about: The FSF funded GNU tool development and defended copyleft licenses — anchoring the free software movement legally and institutionally beyond Stallman's manifesto.

narrative.whyChosen: The FSF gave the free software movement durable organizational backing.
narrative.whyImportant: It sustained GNU development and GPL enforcement for decades.
narrative.problemSolved: Individual activists could not maintain large free software projects alone.

events.title: Intel 80386 introduced
events.summary: Intel introduced the 80386 microprocessor in October 1985 — the first 32-bit x86 CPU with protected mode and virtual memory.
events.about: The 386 enabled true multitasking on PCs — Linux and Windows NT targeted it; OS/2 and early Windows 3.x exploited protected mode. Software could address 4 GB of RAM and run multiple programs safely. Every modern x86 desktop and server still carries 386-era architectural DNA in compatibility mode.

narrative.whyChosen: The 80386 was the chip that made 32-bit personal computing and modern OS design practical on x86.
narrative.whyImportant: It unlocked protected-mode operating systems and set the x86 baseline for decades.
narrative.problemSolved: 16-bit x86 could not efficiently run multitasking OSes with large address spaces.
